name: Nanofluid EOR
principle: Nanoparticles (silica, zirconia, alumina) added to injection water alter rock wettability, lower interfacial tension and build a structural disjoining-pressure wedge. A 2025 review reports lab recoveries of 15 to 20% extra, an optimum concentration of 0.1 to 0.5 wt%, and only a few field trials (a Colombian heavy-oil pilot and Ghawar).

source.note: Journal of Petroleum Exploration and Production Technology, Nanoparticles in enhanced oil recovery: state-of-the-art review (2025; read abstract and body, conclusions truncated)

performance.metric: first field application of nanofluids in thermal EOR (cyclic steam stimulation), two Colombian wells
performance.unit: bbl incremental oil per well (11,966 well A; 3,213 well B); average production increase 97%
performance.basis: functionalized-nanoparticle nanofluid, in-situ upgrading of heavy oil under CSS: post-treatment API gravity 11.6 to 13.4 deg and viscosity 39,987 to 11,734 cP in field; laboratory displacement tests raised recovery from 56% to 76% (lab viscosity to 104 cP, API to 29.2 deg); "production increases averaging 97%"

limitations: Field evidence limited to a few cases
Stability in high salinity and formation damage are open issues
